text:
alex: heads up — sa-east1 apiserver p50/p95 jumped ~2.1s/4.6s right after a bulk gpu provisioning job started. grafana: https://graf.redwood/g/sa-east1-apiserver

sre-oncall-bot: incident created -> INC-2026-1729001111 (priority: medium) :rotating_light:

maria: seeing repeated etcd leader re-election spikes during the window, follower lag goes to 3-5s then catches up. suspecting peering/NAT churn between zones.

jun: confirmed NAT SNAT exhaustion signs on the bosh-nat-gateway in sa-east1-1 around 03:12 UTC. conntrack counters high.

olga: controller-manager restarted twice during the spike, stacktrace shows grpc dial timeouts to apiserver: 
```
I0219 03:12:18.123 controller.go:312] failed to list pods: rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded desc = context deadline exceeded
```

alex: important — this is happening while gpu-provisioner is doing a 400->1200 card ramp (reserved burst test). we should decide whether to pause the ramp or move it to another region. cost tradeoff vs availability.

maria: logs from etcd show peer disconnects + TLS renegotiation: 
```
2019-02-19 03:12:15.001 etcdserver: failed to send to peer 10.40.3.21: write tcp 10.40.1.11:2379->10.40.3.21:2379: write: connection reset by peer
```

jun: quick mitigation: disabling bulk-provisioning job queue reduces apiserver p50 to ~120ms within 30s. I'm patching provisioner to stagger allocation by zone.

product-kate: any user-facing impact? are requests timing out for customers?

alex: some internal health checks and a small fraction of control plane API calls from Dedicated customers saw 503s for ~2m. Not customer-wide but noisy for autoscalers.

olga: opened PR to add pre-warm conntrack reservations & nat-conntrack threshold alerting: https://git.redwood/p/provisioner/conntrack-prewarm

deploy-bot: rollout started: provisioner/staggered-alloc v2 -> canary (50%)

maria: additional follow-ups:
- ask networking to check inter-zone peering throughput and MTU fragmentation for sa-east1 (we saw MSS reductions)
- add controller-manager backoff on apiserver 5xx -> reduce churn
- look at kube-proxy SNAT rules and whether we can use node-local egress for provisioner control plane traffic

jun: quick numbers — cost impact of moving the burst to us-east1 (reserve GPUs for 2h) ~+$6k but avoids risking controlplane instability. we should weigh against SLA exposure.

alex: decision: pause further bulk ramps in sa-east1 until network team signs off. incremental canaries allowed with pace limit. jun, maria — run postmortem blameless note and include prov config and conntrack histograms.

olga: adding pager rule to trigger at conntrack > 80% used or etcd follower lag > 2s for >1m.

sre-oncall-bot: INC-2026-1729001111 status -> mitigated; monitoring will watch for 2h window. :white_check_mark:

jun: will follow up with cost calc and recommendation for pre-warming NAT devices next week.

alex: thanks everyone. keeping this thread open for the postmortem and config diffs.
